html:
English novelist, born in Portsmouth in 1812, whose stories showed the poverty and injustice of Victorian London and helped push for reform.

His childhood marked him. When he was twelve his father was jailed for debt in the Marshalsea prison, and Charles was sent to work in a factory pasting labels on pots of boot polish. Poor children, debtors' prisons and cruel institutions fill his books.

He became famous in his twenties with The Pickwick Papers. His novels came out in monthly or weekly parts, so huge audiences waited for each instalment. Among them:

  • Oliver Twist, an orphan in the workhouse and among thieves
  • A Christmas Carol, which shaped how the English keep Christmas
  • David Copperfield, his most personal book
  • Great Expectations and Bleak House

He was also a journalist and gave dramatic public readings in Britain and America. He wrote in the age of industrialisation and its crowded cities. Dostoevsky admired him. He died in 1870 and is buried in Westminster Abbey.
